---
title: "Install the software you need"
---

Try to do this **before the course starts**, so supervision time can be spent
on the analysis.

You need two kinds of software: **command-line tools** (alignment, peak
calling, coverage tracks) and **R with Bioconductor** (downstream analysis).

## 1. Command-line tools with conda

Install [Miniforge](https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge) (it provides
`conda` and `mamba` with the conda-forge channel preconfigured). Then create
the course environment:

```bash
mamba create -n epigenetics -c conda-forge -c bioconda \
  "samtools>=1.16" htslib bedtools bowtie2 macs3 deeptools fastp multiqc ucsc-bedgraphtobigwig
  # ... add tools here as the material is written
mamba activate epigenetics
```

<!-- Candidates as units are written: bismark, methyldackel (methylation);
     homer, meme (motifs); tobias (footprinting); cooler, pairtools,
     hicexplorer, cooltools (Hi-C); seacr (CUT&Tag); modkit (nanopore). -->

## 2. A genome browser

Install [IGV](https://igv.org/doc/desktop/) (desktop), or use
[igv.js in the browser](https://igv.org/app/).

## 3. R and Bioconductor

Install a recent [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) (4.4 or newer) and
[RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "BiocManager", "torch", "patchwork", "ggrepel", "pheatmap", "data.table"))
torch::install_torch()   # downloads the libtorch backend once (CPU version)
BiocManager::install(c(
  "GenomicRanges",   # genomic intervals
  "rtracklayer",     # read/write BED, narrowPeak, GTF, bigWig
  "Biostrings",      # DNA sequences, CpG counts (What is epigenetics?)
  "Rsamtools",       # indexed FASTA and BAM access
  "GenomicAlignments", # reads from BAM files
  "DESeq2", "edgeR", "apeglm",   # differential accessibility
  "JASPAR2024", "TFBSTools", "motifmatchr", "universalmotif", "RSQLite",  # motifs
  "chromVAR"         # motif accessibility per sample
  # ... add Bioconductor packages here as the material is written
))
```

## 4. Check it works

```bash
mamba activate epigenetics
samtools --version | head -1
macs3 --version
```

```r
library(GenomicRanges)
gr <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(100, 150), width = 100))
reduce(gr)   # should print one merged interval, chr1:100-249
```

If both print without error, you are ready for the course!
